checklist.evidence: Integers in the currency's smallest unit (`bigint`) plus the ISO-4217 code... Rounding happens once per line, half-up
Append-only double-entry ledger... Updates and deletes are blocked, and corrections are reversing entries. Finalized invoices never change; corrections are credit notes.
Exactly one PaymentIntent per invoice, created with the invoice ID as its idempotency key... handle duplicates and out-of-order events by re-fetching the object
Card details are collected only through Stripe Elements and SetupIntents, so we hold `pm_…` tokens and never a card number.
Postgres row-level security (RLS) is forced on, the app role doesn't own the tables... CI rejects any migration that adds a table without RLS
duplicates are dropped by `(tenant_id, event_id)` for 35 days... official numbers are recomputed from raw events at period close
Month-end start dates clamp: Jan 31, then Feb 28, then back to Mar 31... a price can't change once it's been used, so editing creates a new version
take the next gap-free invoice number from a per-tenant, per-series counter row... Anrok or Avalara behind the `TaxProvider` interface
retry schedules per tenant based on decline codes, never retrying hard declines; moves subscriptions from `past_due` to `unpaid` or `canceled`
Daily PSP reconciliation matches every Stripe balance transaction to a ledger posting by PSP ID, and anything unmatched in either direction pages someone.
An entitlements API: build when tenants ask to gate product features by plan in real time.
Build the core: catalog, subscriptions, metering, rating, invoicing and the ledger... If this is billing for your own SaaS, flip the whole gate: buy Stripe Billing or Chargebee
